quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that form the most concise accurate summary, in order.
quests.story: In March the Ridgeway Cycling Club noticed that its Saturday rides were losing members: attendance had fallen from thirty-five to nineteen over a year. A survey of former members, sent by the secretary, Ms. Adler, showed that most found the pace too fast and the routes too long. The committee introduced two groups, a relaxed fifteen-mile ride and a faster thirty-mile ride, both leaving at nine from the same car park. By September attendance had climbed to forty-four.
options: By September attendance had climbed to forty-four.
Attendance at the Ridgeway Cycling Club's Saturday rides fell from thirty-five to nineteen in a year.
A survey sent by the secretary, Ms. Adler, asked former members about the routes, and both rides left at nine from the same car park.
A survey showed former members found the pace too fast and the routes too long, so the committee introduced a relaxed ride and a faster one.
quests.hint: A good summary keeps the cause and effect, not the logistics.
quests.explanation: The survey's sender and the start time are true but minor, and they leave out why the rides changed. The summary needs the drop, the survey-driven split, and the recovery.
storyKeyEvents: Attendance at the Ridgeway Cycling Club's Saturday rides fell from thirty-five to nineteen in a year.
A survey showed former members found the pace too fast and the routes too long, so the committee introduced a relaxed ride and a faster one.
By September attendance had climbed to forty-four.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: The new library app lets members renew books and reserve study rooms. In its first month eight hundred members installed it, about a fifth of all members. Staff noticed that renewals at the desk dropped by a third, which freed up an hour a day to help visitors with research questions. The librarian called the app a useful addition but admitted that older members still preferred the desk.
options: The librarian called the app useful but said older members still preferred the desk.
The librarian called the app an essential addition to the library and said that older members had now stopped using the desk altogether.
Desk renewals dropped by a third, freeing about an hour a day for research help.
The library's new app let members renew books and reserve study rooms, and about a fifth of members installed it in the first month.
quests.hint: Watch for words that make a claim stronger than the author's.
quests.explanation: The librarian said "useful", not "essential", and older members still preferred the desk. The altered statement strengthens one claim and reverses another.
storyKeyEvents: The library's new app let members renew books and reserve study rooms, and about a fifth of members installed it in the first month.
Desk renewals dropped by a third, freeing about an hour a day for research help.
The librarian called the app useful but said older members still preferred the desk.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: The council resurfaced Albert Street in July, closing it to traffic for three weeks. Shops reported a fall in sales of about a fifth, and the council offered them a rates rebate. When the street reopened, footfall returned to its usual level within a week. The council said it would publish a report on the project's costs in the autumn.
options: Albert Street was closed to traffic for three weeks for resurfacing, and shops reported sales falling by about a fifth.
Footfall returned to its usual level within a week of the street reopening.
The council offered the shops a rates rebate.
The council's disastrous closure of Albert Street ruined local shops.
quests.hint: Look for a judgement that the author never makes.
quests.explanation: "Disastrous" and "ruined" are opinions, and the shops' footfall recovered within a week. A fair summary reports the closure, the rebate and the recovery.
storyKeyEvents: Albert Street was closed to traffic for three weeks for resurfacing, and shops reported sales falling by about a fifth.
The council offered the shops a rates rebate.
Footfall returned to its usual level within a week of the street reopening.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: Dara's group project on renewable energy had three members, but one, Kofi, missed the first two meetings. Dara reallocated the workload so that Kofi took over the data charts, which suited his skills, and scheduled shorter, more frequent meetings. Kofi attended every meeting after that and finished his charts early. The group received a mark of 72, their best of the term, although the tutor noted that the conclusion was thin.
options: Kofi attended every later meeting and the group earned 72, their best mark of the term.
Dara gave Kofi the data charts and scheduled shorter, more frequent meetings.
The group earned a perfect mark and full praise.
Dara's group project suffered when Kofi missed the first two meetings.
quests.hint: Compare the mark and the tutor's comment with the story's.
quests.explanation: The group earned 72, not full marks, and the tutor called the conclusion thin. The statement inflates both the mark and the praise.
storyKeyEvents: Dara's group project suffered when Kofi missed the first two meetings.
Dara gave Kofi the data charts and scheduled shorter, more frequent meetings.
Kofi attended every later meeting and the group earned 72, their best mark of the term.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: When the ferry timetable changed, the island's post office lost its daily delivery. The postmaster, Mr. Bell, asked the ferry company to carry mail bags on the early boat, and they agreed for a small fee. A neighbour, Ms. Quill, volunteered to sort the bags at the pier. Deliveries to the island resumed within a week, and letters arrived by nine each morning.
options: Deliveries resumed within a week, with letters arriving by nine each morning.
Ms. Quill, a neighbour, volunteered to sort the mail bags at the pier, and her help saved the delivery.
A new ferry timetable cost the island's post office its daily delivery.
The postmaster arranged for the ferry company to carry mail on the early boat for a small fee.
quests.hint: Who solved the main problem, and who only helped along the way?
quests.explanation: Ms. Quill's sorting was a helpful extra, but the delivery was restored by the postmaster's arrangement with the ferry. The statement promotes her to the centre of the story.
storyKeyEvents: A new ferry timetable cost the island's post office its daily delivery.
The postmaster arranged for the ferry company to carry mail on the early boat for a small fee.
Deliveries resumed within a week, with letters arriving by nine each morning.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: A food festival on the town green had to be postponed when heavy rain waterlogged the ground. The organisers moved it to the following Saturday and asked stallholders to confirm by email. Sixty of the seventy stallholders confirmed, and the rest were replaced from a waiting list. On the new date the festival drew around four thousand visitors, and a local radio station interviewed the mayor on site.
options: A local radio station interviewed the mayor at the festival.
A food festival was postponed when rain waterlogged the town green.
The organisers moved it to the following Saturday and filled the vacant stalls from a waiting list.
On the new date around four thousand visitors came.
quests.hint: An interesting extra at the end isn't the outcome.
quests.explanation: The interview is a side event and doesn't describe how the festival turned out. The outcome is the crowd on the new date.
storyKeyEvents: A food festival was postponed when rain waterlogged the town green.
The organisers moved it to the following Saturday and filled the vacant stalls from a waiting list.
On the new date around four thousand visitors came.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: After three complaints about slow service, the manager of the Harbour Café reviewed the order system. She found that orders written on paper were often misread in the kitchen. She introduced a tablet system that sent orders directly to a screen, and waiting times fell from twenty minutes to twelve. The waiters said the screens were easy to learn, and two new staff were trained in a morning.
options: Tablet order systems make every café faster.
She introduced a tablet system that sent orders straight to a kitchen screen.
Waiting times fell from twenty minutes to twelve.
After complaints about slow service, the Harbour Café's manager found that paper orders were often misread in the kitchen.
quests.hint: A conclusion about all cafés goes beyond a story about one.
quests.explanation: The story reports one café's results, so a claim about every café generalises beyond the evidence. The accurate summary stays with the Harbour Café.
storyKeyEvents: After complaints about slow service, the Harbour Café's manager found that paper orders were often misread in the kitchen.
She introduced a tablet system that sent orders straight to a kitchen screen.
Waiting times fell from twenty minutes to twelve.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: Clara's company lost a major client in January after a late delivery. A review found that the delay began when a supplier's invoice was filed in the wrong folder, but the main cause was that no one was responsible for checking incoming deliveries. Clara appointed a delivery coordinator and set a weekly check. By June the company had won back a smaller contract from the client.
options: Clara's company lost a major client after a late delivery.
The delivery was late because one invoice was filed in the wrong folder.
A review found the main cause was that nobody was responsible for checking incoming deliveries, so Clara appointed a coordinator.
By June the company had won back a smaller contract from the client.
quests.hint: Which cause does the review call the main one?
quests.explanation: The misfiled invoice was where the delay began, but the review names the lack of responsibility as the main cause. The statement puts the smaller trigger in the place of the main cause.
storyKeyEvents: Clara's company lost a major client after a late delivery.
A review found the main cause was that nobody was responsible for checking incoming deliveries, so Clara appointed a coordinator.
By June the company had won back a smaller contract from the client.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: The school's after-school club was oversubscribed, with sixty children competing for thirty places. The head teacher asked parents for volunteers to supervise, and twelve responded. With the extra supervisors the school could open a second room and accept all sixty children. Parents also asked for a club in the holidays, which the school said it would consider.
options: Twelve parents volunteered to supervise when the head teacher asked.
With the extra supervisors a second room opened and all sixty children were accepted.
The after-school club had sixty children competing for thirty places.
The school opened a second room, which led twelve parents to volunteer.
quests.hint: Check which happened first, and which made the other possible.
quests.explanation: The volunteers came first, and their help made the second room possible. The altered statement reverses cause and effect.
storyKeyEvents: The after-school club had sixty children competing for thirty places.
Twelve parents volunteered to supervise when the head teacher asked.
With the extra supervisors a second room opened and all sixty children were accepted.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: Orla's book club moved from a pub to a library room after the pub raised its room fee. The move cost nothing, and the library offered free tea. Attendance stayed at twelve members, but two members said they missed the pub's atmosphere. The club agreed to review the decision in six months.
options: The club moved to the library to stop two members drinking during meetings.
Attendance stayed at twelve, and the club agreed to review the decision in six months.
The book club left the pub when it raised its room fee.
The club moved to a free library room that offered free tea.
quests.hint: Stick to the reason the author gives for the move.
quests.explanation: The story gives the pub's room fee as the reason. Stopping members drinking is an intention nobody states.
storyKeyEvents: The book club left the pub when it raised its room fee.
The club moved to a free library room that offered free tea.
Attendance stayed at twelve, and the club agreed to review the decision in six months.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that form the most concise accurate summary, in order.
quests.story: The parish church's bell tower developed a crack after a cold winter. An engineer surveyed it on a Tuesday and recommended steel braces, at a cost of twelve thousand pounds. The congregation held a summer fair, a sponsored walk and a raffle, and raised fourteen thousand. The braces were fitted in October, and the bells rang again at Christmas.
options: The congregation raised £14,000 through a summer fair, a sponsored walk and a raffle.
An engineer surveyed the crack on a Tuesday, and the congregation held events over the summer, including a fair and a raffle.
The church bell tower cracked after a cold winter, and an engineer recommended steel braces costing £12,000.
The braces were fitted in October and the bells rang again at Christmas.
quests.hint: A good summary says what the events achieved, not just that they took place.
quests.explanation: The survey day and the vague "events" give detail without the cost, the amount raised or the result. The summary needs the recommended repair, the money raised, and the ringing bells.
storyKeyEvents: The church bell tower cracked after a cold winter, and an engineer recommended steel braces costing £12,000.
The congregation raised £14,000 through a summer fair, a sponsored walk and a raffle.
The braces were fitted in October and the bells rang again at Christmas.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: A survey of a hundred commuters found that the number 7 bus was late more often than any other route. The bus company adjusted two timetable stops and added a bus at peak times. On-time performance rose from seventy per cent to eighty-two. Commuters said the service was better, though several still wanted real-time tracking.
options: A survey found the number 7 bus was late more often than any other route.
On-time performance rose from seventy to eighty-two per cent, though several commuters still wanted real-time tracking.
Commuters said the service had become perfect and no longer wanted any changes.
The company adjusted two timetable stops and added a peak-time bus.
quests.hint: Look at what the commuters still wanted.
quests.explanation: Several commuters still wanted real-time tracking, so the service wasn't called perfect. The statement removes the reservation the author reports.
storyKeyEvents: A survey found the number 7 bus was late more often than any other route.
The company adjusted two timetable stops and added a peak-time bus.
On-time performance rose from seventy to eighty-two per cent, though several commuters still wanted real-time tracking.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: The company's new open-plan office opened in April. Staff reported more interruptions, and a noise survey showed levels above the recommended limit in two areas. The manager added quiet booths and set a rule for phone calls. Two months later the number of noise complaints had dropped by half.
options: Staff reported more interruptions in the new open-plan office, and a noise survey showed levels above the limit in two areas.
The manager added quiet booths and a rule for phone calls.
The badly designed open-plan office was a foolish idea from the start.
Noise complaints dropped by half within two months.
quests.hint: An opinion word like "foolish" isn't part of a neutral summary.
quests.explanation: The author reports figures and changes, not a verdict, and the complaints fell after the fixes. The judgement is added by the statement.
storyKeyEvents: Staff reported more interruptions in the new open-plan office, and a noise survey showed levels above the limit in two areas.
The manager added quiet booths and a rule for phone calls.
Noise complaints dropped by half within two months.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: Hassan's new delivery firm started with two vans. A local supermarket offered him a contract for morning deliveries, and he hired a third driver to cover it. Within a year his firm delivered to forty shops, and he bought a fourth van. He said the growth had been faster than he expected but steady.
options: Hassan's delivery firm started with two vans.
Within a year the firm served forty shops and had a fourth van.
A supermarket's morning delivery contract led him to hire a third driver.
Within a year Hassan's firm became the region's largest delivery company.
quests.hint: Check how big the result the story reports really is.
quests.explanation: Forty shops and four vans is growth, but the story never says his firm was the region's largest. The statement inflates the outcome.
storyKeyEvents: Hassan's delivery firm started with two vans.
A supermarket's morning delivery contract led him to hire a third driver.
Within a year the firm served forty shops and had a fourth van.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: The theatre's annual costume sale was in danger because the storeroom flooded. The manager, Ms. Dupont, moved the undamaged costumes to the foyer and arranged for the damaged ones to be cleaned by a specialist. A volunteer, Mr. Acker, made a new price list. The sale went ahead a week later and raised three thousand pounds.
options: Ms. Dupont moved the undamaged costumes to the foyer and had the damaged ones professionally cleaned.
The sale went ahead a week later and raised £3,000.
A flood in the storeroom endangered the theatre's annual costume sale.
Mr. Acker, a volunteer, made a new price list that saved the sale.
quests.hint: A helper's task isn't the same as what saved the event.
quests.explanation: The price list is a helpful task, but the sale was rescued by moving and cleaning the costumes. The statement gives a minor helper the main credit.
storyKeyEvents: A flood in the storeroom endangered the theatre's annual costume sale.
Ms. Dupont moved the undamaged costumes to the foyer and had the damaged ones professionally cleaned.
The sale went ahead a week later and raised £3,000.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that form the most concise accurate summary, in order.
quests.story: The students' union wanted to reduce single-use cups on campus. It gave a free reusable cup to every first-year and offered a twenty-pence discount on drinks for anyone who brought one. After a term, sales of single-use cups had fallen by forty per cent. Separately, the union's shop reported a rise in sales of reusable bottles.
options: After a term single-use cup sales had fallen by forty per cent.
It gave every first-year a free reusable cup and a 20p discount for bringing one.
The union's shop reported a rise in sales of reusable bottles.
The students' union wanted to reduce single-use cups on campus.
quests.hint: "Separately" signals an extra, not the outcome.
quests.explanation: The bottle sales are a side result and don't say whether the cup scheme worked. The outcome is the forty per cent fall in single-use cups.
storyKeyEvents: The students' union wanted to reduce single-use cups on campus.
It gave every first-year a free reusable cup and a 20p discount for bringing one.
After a term single-use cup sales had fallen by forty per cent.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.
quests.story: When Esther started mentoring a new colleague, the two met for thirty minutes every Thursday. Esther asked the colleague to choose a topic each week and to summarise what she learned at the end. After three months the colleague led her first client meeting, and Esther's manager asked her to mentor another newcomer.
options: Esther mentored a new colleague in weekly thirty-minute sessions on topics the colleague chose.
Weekly mentoring always turns newcomers into confident leaders within three months.
After three months the colleague led her first client meeting, and Esther was asked to mentor another newcomer.
The colleague summarised what she learned at the end of each session.
quests.hint: Does the story claim something about all newcomers, or about one?
quests.explanation: It reports one colleague's progress, and "always" turns that into a rule about everyone. A faithful summary stays with the single case.
storyKeyEvents: Esther mentored a new colleague in weekly thirty-minute sessions on topics the colleague chose.
The colleague summarised what she learned at the end of each session.
After three months the colleague led her first client meeting, and Esther was asked to mentor another newcomer.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.

Analysis showed that customers had received the wrong size in a quarter of the cases and that the size chart on the website was out of date. The manager updated the chart and added a size-check step at packing. The packer's shift pattern had also changed in May. By July returns had fallen to their usual level.
options: By July returns were back to their usual level.
The manager updated the out-of-date size chart and added a size check at packing.
An online shop's returns rose sharply in May, with wrong sizes in a quarter of the cases.
Returns rose as the packer's shifts changed.
quests.hint: Which cause did the analysis point to?
quests.explanation: The shift change happened at the same time, but the analysis pointed to wrong sizes and an out-of-date chart. The statement swaps a coincidence for the real cause.
storyKeyEvents: An online shop's returns rose sharply in May, with wrong sizes in a quarter of the cases.
The manager updated the out-of-date size chart and added a size check at packing.
By July returns were back to their usual level.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.

options: The committee had an energy audit done because the glazing was fitted.
The committee fitted secondary glazing for £3,000.
The village hall's heating bills doubled, and an energy audit found the windows leaked heat.
The next winter's bills fell by a third.
quests.hint: Which came first: the audit or the glazing?
quests.explanation: The audit found the leaks, and then the glazing was fitted. The statement turns the order and the reason round.
storyKeyEvents: The village hall's heating bills doubled, and an energy audit found the windows leaked heat.
The committee fitted secondary glazing for £3,000.
The next winter's bills fell by a third.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.

options: Subscribers rose to ninety, and the organisers would wait for another season's data before adding delivery.
The cooperative began selling vegetable boxes by subscription and had fifty subscribers, mostly within five miles.
The cooperative added the station pick-up to undercut a rival supermarket.
It added a pick-up point at the railway station.

storyKeyEvents: The cooperative began selling vegetable boxes by subscription and had fifty subscribers, mostly within five miles.
It added a pick-up point at the railway station.
Subscribers rose to ninety, and the organisers would wait for another season's data before adding delivery.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that form the most concise accurate summary, in order.

options: Lina used a phone app to measure the volume and apologised to residents in a letter.
The president found the volume above the agreed limit and fitted a volume limiter.
No further complaints were received.
The radio society received a complaint that its late-night show was too loud for the neighbouring flats.

storyKeyEvents: The radio society received a complaint that its late-night show was too loud for the neighbouring flats.
The president found the volume above the agreed limit and fitted a volume limiter.
No further complaints were received.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.

options: A triage nurse was assigned at the door to sort patients by urgency.
Waits fell almost to nothing; satisfaction soared.
The hospital's outpatient clinic had an average wait of fifty minutes.
Waits fell to thirty-five minutes and satisfaction improved slightly.

storyKeyEvents: The hospital's outpatient clinic had an average wait of fifty minutes.
A triage nurse was assigned at the door to sort patients by urgency.
Waits fell to thirty-five minutes and satisfaction improved slightly.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.

options: The paper's chaotic, overcrowded newsroom was a disaster that hurt its reporters, its editors and its readers alike.
The paper kept the layout, and online readership grew by twelve per cent.
A regional newspaper moved its reporters into a shared newsroom to save rent.
Editors said conversations across desks helped share leads, and a quiet room was added for writing.

storyKeyEvents: A regional newspaper moved its reporters into a shared newsroom to save rent.
Editors said conversations across desks helped share leads, and a quiet room was added for writing.
The paper kept the layout, and online readership grew by twelve per cent.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.

Sunday footfall doubled and every shop extended its opening hours.
The town introduced free Sunday parking in the high street.

Sunday footfall rose eight per cent and two cafés extended their hours, while the council lost about £9,000 in parking income.
The council decided to continue the scheme for another year.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.

A parent offered to donate some old balls, which solved the shortage.
The school introduced a lock-up rota for the caretaker.
Replacement kit arrived within two weeks.

The school introduced a lock-up rota for the caretaker.
Replacement kit arrived within two weeks.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that form the most concise accurate summary, in order.

The council wanted to reduce litter in the park.
Litter collected by the council fell by a third over the summer.
The park café's sales rose in the summer.

Litter collected by the council fell by a third over the summer.

quests.instruction: One statement changes or adds to what the author says. Arrange the other three in order.

His manager suggested Friday walking meetings, which the team tried for six weeks.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that preserve cause, effect and outcome without excess detail, in order.
quests.story: The city library's visitor numbers fell by a fifth over two years. options: Visitors fell because the building's decor was dated, and the library redecorated.
The city library's visitor numbers fell by a fifth over two years.
